statement: REPRESENTATIVE RETAINED-ONLY EXPERT RECOVERY SINGLE-USE RELEASE V1 APPROVED

correction.defect: The v1 artifact substantively approved this release with zero BLOCKING and zero NON_BLOCKING_REQUIRED findings but emitted verdict APPROVE. The committed release wrapper authorize() (scripts/research/f017_representative_expert_recovery_release_wrapper_v1.py line 49) fail-closes unless approval.verdict is exactly ACCEPT, so v1 is not executable approval authority; pointing the wrapper at v1 raises INDEPENDENT_RELEASE_GATE.
correction.resolution: Independent full re-verification of the identical release bytes and authority chain at head 1163182399a2148579029213caf325684b71e350 (v1 reviewed 23d73e51a5def638b72e73a61c982bad3d8bd2a4; the single intervening commit adds only the banked v1 artifact itself, no code). This v2 artifact re-issues the same substantive approval with the wrapper-compatible verdict token ACCEPT. v1 is retained unmodified append-only as the historical record; v2 supersedes v1 as the sole executable approval authority for this release.

approval_scope_declaration: This approval does not execute anything and is not computation. It performed no checkpoint access, no shard opens, no retained-payload opens, no decoder invocation, and no expert computation; checkpoint access remains prohibited and the real payload ledger remains 175 with zero movement under any outcome. A separate machine-local byte-exact 8-field GO token (approval_sha256, attempt_id, authorization_sha256, disposition GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY, event_id, real_event_authorized, release_id, release_sha256) is still required and was not created here; the approval_sha256 token field must bind this v2 file's sha256, not the superseded v1 artifact. This document approves exactly one retained-only representative expert-recovery execution of release F017-REPRESENTATIVE-M1F0-EXPERT-OUTPUT-RECOVERY-1-RELEASE-1 through the bound release wrapper in the pinned environment, stopping after eight individual expert outputs before any weighted aggregate; it authorizes nothing else, no second attempt, no retry, no resume, and no downstream aggregation, shared-expert, FFN-completion, or S2 authority.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Carried FC-DID-1..FC-DID-7 from the banked final composition review (aeda9f78...)
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The seven adjudicated defense-in-depth observations (environment not echoed into durable records; terminalizer does not separately record manifest.json; go-token synthesizable from committed bytes with path-relative one-shot enforcement under honest-operator threat model; executor transitively imports the module containing the sole checkpoint capability class with zero references; validator binds three helpers to self-declared hashes and is itself unpinned; --internal-reproduce gated only by an environment variable when invoked directly; validator plain-JSON parse, pre-attempt-start crash window, CPU_ONLY without runtime check) remain accurately characterized and non-blocking at the re-reviewed head: none can mint committed authority, move the ledger, open a checkpoint or shard, or bypass the byte-exact release_sha256 and approval pins on the authoritative wrapper path.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Release id_weight_pairs are pair objects while the authorization stores parallel arrays
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The authorization has no id_weight_pairs key; it carries output_contract.canonical_order and routing_weights as parallel arrays. Independent recomputation at the re-reviewed head confirmed every release pair (ordinal, expert_id, routing_weight) is exactly consistent with those arrays and with selected_expert_ids, so the atomic pairing is faithful; the representational difference is noted only because a naive object-equality comparison between the two contracts returns false.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Wrapper approval gate checks only verdict, release_sha256, and release_id on the approval object
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: authorize() validates the operator-supplied approval file solely via verdict==ACCEPT, release_sha256, and release_id top-level fields; it does not check schema, statement, or blocking-finding emptiness. The go-token's approval_sha256 field byte-pins the approval file, and a tree sweep at the re-reviewed head confirmed no other committed JSON carries verdict ACCEPT together with top-level release_sha256 ccf33fef... and this release_id (the two banked ACCEPT reviews mentioning the release hash have no top-level release_sha256/release_id), so this v2 artifact is the unique committed document that can satisfy the gate. Non-blocking under the honest-operator threat model already adjudicated in FC-DID-3.
